beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: SOLIPSICON places vulnerable children above a world they are pressured to hurt.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their own continued existence depends on machinery and rewards they cannot escape easily.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The philosophical science fiction also follows human experience from inside that pressure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its dual perspective complicates the boundary between a victim and an operator.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A child's dependence can coexist with terrible power over someone else's experience.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel makes that contradiction personal before expanding its account of reality.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Kael wakes as the support of his dimensional nest begins to fail.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: His hunger disperses through a body unlike a human body.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The systems surrounding him translate continued existence into levels and instructions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That opening establishes vulnerability inside the position that appears to hold power.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reader must understand his dependence without letting it erase responsibility.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its unfamiliar embodiment makes that tension harder than an ordinary villain's motive.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The human perspective begins with Mara watching rain beside a clinic window.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its reflection seems to violate what she knows the weather is doing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She must distinguish an altered perception from a disturbance outside herself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel gives that uncertainty mundane surroundings and another person's impatient response.
